title: Cauchy-Schwarz Extensions: Hölder, Bessel, and L² Structure Theorems

problemStatement.formal: Extensions of Cauchy-Schwarz: Hölder's inequality, Bessel's inequality, Pythagorean theorem in L², parallelogram law, polarization identity, weighted CS, AM-GM from CS, L1-L2 norm comparison
problemStatement.plain: A comprehensive collection of extensions and consequences of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, including Hölder's inequality for finite sums, Bessel's inequality for orthonormal families, the Pythagorean theorem and parallelogram law in L², and norm comparison theorems.
whyMatters: Hölder's inequality generalizes Cauchy-Schwarz to conjugate exponents p,q
Bessel's inequality is foundational for Fourier analysis and orthogonal expansions
Pythagorean theorem and parallelogram law characterize inner product spaces
These results form the core toolkit of functional analysis

proven: Hölder's inequality for finite sums (NNReal): ∑ f·g ≤ (∑ f^p)^(1/p)·(∑ g^q)^(1/q)
Cauchy-Schwarz as Hölder p=q=2 special case
L² membership ↔ integrability of squared norm
L² inner product integrable: ∫ f·g is well-defined for f,g ∈ L²
L² inner product = integral bridge: ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫ f·g dμ
L² norm squared = integral: ‖f‖² = ∫ f² dμ
Non-negativity of L² norm squared via integral

insights: Weighted CS reduces to standard CS via √w substitution
Bessel proved via projection: p=∑⟨x,eᵢ⟩eᵢ, then ‖x-p‖²≥0
Parallelogram law and polarization are purely algebraic in inner product spaces
